note: From the OpenStreetMap export (main API, 13 October 2026; tools/osm-to-kit.mjs) and the view from above (docs/reference/aerial/ashburys.jpg), 1.25 times real across the line like the tracks. Positive v is north; the line runs west towards Manchester. The real station has two side platforms (about 122 m) on the passenger pair, with a second pair of lines on the north side beyond platform 1 (the freight lines and the Philips Park branch in OpenStreetMap) and the Hope Valley, Glossop and Marple lines parting beyond it to the east; here only the Marple pair is drawn, as the game's two tracks, with a side platform 2.1 m outside each (a game choice). The halt's platform is the real platform 2, on the south side, for trains towards Manchester. The platforms take a four-car train as they are; trains stop 20 m west of the station's point so a two-car one stands on them as they are and a six-car one once they're extended west. The footbridge is at the east end, by the platforms' ends, with steps down to each platform (the way across), and the line crosses Pottery Lane (the A6010) on a bridge just beyond it: drawn as its parapets, the road below left to the ground. The long flight of steps from Pottery Lane up the south side to the halt's platform is real but runs below rail level, so it isn't drawn. The big industrial shed south of the line is from its OpenStreetMap outline (its height a guess); the palisade fence along the north side from OpenStreetMap. The bus stop is Pottery Lane/Ashburys Station (stop A), on Pottery Lane below the bridge. No photographs: the shelters, lamps and boards are the usual Northern ones from memory; no booking office is drawn or offered (from memory the station has none worth the name), and the lifts and canopy are the game's.
